core_obligations: Reduce to the model case (proof lines 9983-9986): the construction of f_* commutes with etale localization and a finite etale morphism is etale locally on source and target a disjoint union of isomorphisms, so it suffices to prove the assertion for the local model.

Close the model case (proof lines 9987-9990): in the model the pullback of locally constant sheaves is a finite product of locally constant sheaves, and the author states and verifies directly that such a product is again (finite) locally constant; the cases of abelian groups and of Lambda-modules are the same verification.
proof_roadmap: Observe that f_* commutes with etale localization.
Replace the finite etale morphism by its local model, a finite disjoint union of isomorphisms.
Conclude that a finite product of locally constant sheaves is locally constant, in each of the three categories.
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the pushforward along a finite etale morphism of schemes preserves (finite) locally constant sheaves of sets, and likewise of abelian groups and of Lambda-modules, on the small etale sites (statement lines 9972-9980). The proof is short but genuine: the author first removes the geometry by observing that f_* commutes with etale localization, and that a finite etale morphism is etale locally a disjoint union of isomorphisms (proof lines 9983-9986), which reduces the assertion to the statement that a finite product of locally constant sheaves is locally constant; the author states that reduced assertion and closes it directly (proof lines 9987-9990), the other two categories being the same argument. The non-formal content is the reduction to the local product model. The claim is H1: a short reduction followed by a direct verification.
